cases.input: A note transfers from holder A to holder B.
cases.expect: Instrument identity and terms persist while positions and holder capacities change.

cases.input: A note converts under versioned cap, discount and ratio terms.
cases.expect: An explicit event retires the predecessor position and creates successor positions against the resulting instrument version.

cases.input: A mutable ticker is used as sole instrument identity.
cases.expect: The identity is rejected without a governed identifier.
cases.violates: The identity is rejected without a governed identifier.

cases.input: Contingent conversion rights are counted as current votes.
cases.expect: The denominator calculation is rejected.

cases.input: A high valuation is used to establish control.
cases.expect: The inference is rejected.

cases.input: Conversion terms are edited in an issued version.
cases.expect: The mutation is rejected; a successor version is required.
cases.violates: The mutation is rejected; a successor version is required.

cases.input: A convertible note's cap, discount and ratio terms are recorded on the WM-ECO-038 position record, and the position identity is used as the instrument identity.
cases.expect: Rejected. Terms resolve only to an InstrumentVersion; WM-ECO-038 masters positions, quantities, lots, rights, restrictions and successor history only.
cases.violates: WM-ECO-038 owns security-backed positions only; instrument identity is independent

cases.input: Instrument I-1 version v2 carries equity terms for share classes A and B with differing vote ratios.
cases.expect: Accepted. Both classes are subordinate classifications within InstrumentVersion v2; neither acquires instrument, position or holding identity.

cases.input: Share Class B is allocated an independent root and a position is bound to it instead of to an instrument version.
cases.expect: Rejected. Share Class never masters instrument, position, holding or investment identity.
cases.violates: Share Class is a subordinate classification

cases.input: A note's terms are mastered simultaneously by WM-ECO-037 and by Financial Instrument, with divergent maturity values.
cases.expect: Rejected. Dual term mastership is not permitted; the specialization direction is unadjudicated and no shared term model may be asserted.
cases.violates: WM-ECO-037 specialization undecided; no rival master

cases.input: An instrument registry record states a maturity differing from the issuer's InstrumentVersion, and the registry value is written over the issuer value.
cases.expect: Rejected. Issuer masters terms; the registry masters the governed identifier only; the divergence is retained as a recorded conflict state.
cases.violates: Mastership precedence; conflicts are never silently reconciled

cases.input: InstrumentVersion v1 records a conversion right in the same untyped rights collection as voting and dividend rights, with no contingency field.
cases.expect: Rejected. Every right is typed present or contingent; a contingent right requires trigger, effectTimeRule and excludedFromDenominators true.

cases.input: A consumer sums present voting rights and an unexercised conversion right from InstrumentVersion v1 into one rights total.
cases.expect: Rejected. Contingent rights are never emitted, serialized or aggregated as present rights.
cases.violates: Contingent rights are not present rights

cases.input: Instrument N has v1 effective 2026-01-01 to 2026-08-15 and v2 effective from 2026-08-15; the version in force at 2026-06-30 is requested.
cases.expect: v1 is returned, resolved from effective intervals alone and independently of any derivedCurrentVersionRef.

cases.input: derivedCurrentVersionRef is treated as the authoritative source of the version in force, or is required for resolution.
cases.expect: Rejected. It is a non-authoritative cache; resolution is from effective intervals.

cases.input: Instrument N records v2 effective from 2026-06-01 while v1 remains effective to 2026-08-15.
cases.expect: Rejected. Effective intervals of versions of one instrument never overlap.

cases.input: A corrected version is written back as v2 after v2 was already issued, or version numbering decreases.
cases.expect: Rejected. Version numbers increase monotonically and are never reused; correction creates a successor version.

cases.input: The conversion cap on issued version v1 is edited in place.
cases.expect: Rejected. Terms are immutable after issuance; a successor version with its own effectiveFrom, recordedAt, knowledgeTime and contentDigest is required, and v1 remains resolvable.
cases.violates: Instrument terms are immutable and versioned

cases.input: Note N v1 is held in two lots H-1a and H-1b; only H-1a converts on 2026-08-15 to preferred position H-2 against v2.
cases.expect: H-1a is derecognized with predecessor/successor lineage and linked postings; H-1b remains outstanding against v1; instrument state remains effective; H-1b's cost lineage and restrictions are unchanged.

cases.input: Instrument N is set to state converted after H-1a converts while H-1b remains outstanding.
cases.expect: Rejected. converted is reachable only when every outstanding position has been derecognized by a conversion event.
cases.violates: No unsafe inference of full conversion

cases.input: Conversion of note N writes successorRef on N pointing to the preferred-share instrument.
cases.expect: Rejected. successorRef records corporate-action instrument replacement only; conversion creates no instrument successorRef and the participation, not the instrument, carries continuity.

holds: Expectations are reviewable-draft adjudications over non-canonical bases and assert no conformance, installability or standards alignment.
